When multiple writes happen at once
column2: we may need to sacrifice a currently

column1: active block group to be zone finished for a new allocation. We choose a
block group with the least free space left
To do the finishing
column2: we need to send IOs for already allocated region

column1: and wait for them and on-going IOs. Otherwise
zone is already finished at the time the IO reach a device.
However
column2: if a block group dedicated to the data relocation is zone

column1: finished
column2: there is a chance that finishing it before an ongoing write IO

column1: reaches the device. That is because there is timing gap between an
allocation is done (block_group->reservations == 0
done) and an ordered extent is created when the relocation IO starts.
Thus
column2: if we finish the zone between them

column1: We cannot simply use ""fs_info->data_reloc_bg == block_group->start"" to
avoid the zone finishing. Because
column2: the data_reloc_bg may already switch to

column1: a new block group
column2: while there are still ongoing write IOs to the old

column1: data_reloc_bg.
So
column2: this patch reworks the BLOCK_GROUP_FLAG_ZONED_DATA_RELOC bit to

column1: indicate there is a data relocation allocation and/or ongoing write to the
block group. The bit is set on allocation and cleared in end_io function of
the last IO for the currently allocated region.
To change the timing of the bit setting also solves the issue that the bit
being left even after there is no IO going on. With the current code
the data_reloc_bg switches after the last IO to the current data_reloc_bg
the bit is set at this timing and there is no one clearing that bit. As a
result
column2: that block group is kept unallocatable for anything.
